clue.text: Not physically fit, but willing to participate

definitions.meaning: a lame or injured one, so the word can mean disabled
someone who is up for anything is said to be ready and eager to join in

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: an injured, lame limb, and being keen or up for a challenge.

clue.text: Great Detective Agency receives bill it rejected — that leaves a sour taste

indicators.note: the outer pieces take in the inner run, as a recipient takes delivery

parts.note: ace is slang for great or excellent
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the two words are read backwards

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
taken as written

explanation.surface: A famous firm of private eyes gets an invoice it sends back, leaving a bitter aftertaste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' gives TICA, which 'receives' places between the two halves of the outer charade. CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detective branch, which is how it stands for a detective agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetic acid is the compound that gives vinegar its sharp sour flavour.

clue.text: Final customer puts up with swapping a couple of positions

indicators.note: two letters change places, the R and the S trading spots in the synonym

parts.note: to endure something is to put up with it

explanation.surface: The last buyer in a chain tolerates being shuffled between roles.
explanation.walkthrough: In ENDURES, swap the R and the S to get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The end user is the person who finally uses a product, the last customer in the chain.

clue.text: In turn, can choose to cavil

indicators.note: turning the word round reads its letters backwards

parts.note: a tin is a can
to pick is to choose

explanation.surface: One by one, you may select what to complain about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In turn' looks like a link phrase meaning one at a time, but it reverses the can; 'cavil' is a verb, so 'to' belongs with it.
explanation.definitionFit: To nitpick is to find fault over trivial details, which is what cavilling means.

clue.text: Short measure in utterance: cry of horror: not seriously!

parts.note: tongue can mean speech or language, an utterance
an inch is a small unit of length
eek is an exclamation of alarm

explanation.surface: Someone speaking of a skimpy portion yelps in fright, then insists they were only joking.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something tongue-in-cheek means saying it ironically, as a joke rather than in earnest.

clue.text: Strong leggings for men

definitions.meaning: sturdy leather leg coverings worn over trousers by cowboys and riders
informal plural for fellows or blokes

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both protective leather riding leggings and, informally, a group of fellows.

clue.text: Heartily disbelieve endless correspondence I entered into in dungeon

indicators.note: only the heart of the synonym is kept, its first and last letters dropped

parts.note: to doubt is to disbelieve

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the shortened word
the synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: a letter is a piece of correspondence

explanation.surface: Someone sincerely doubts that an unfinished letter was slipped into a prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartily' gives OUB, 'endless' gives LETTE, and 'entered into' turns that into LIETTE. The word comes from French oublier, to forget: prisoners were left there and forgotten.
explanation.definitionFit: An oubliette is a secret dungeon reached only through a trapdoor in its ceiling.

clue.text: Curious respect in which man gets feeling of repulsion

indicators.note: the second piece sits inside the rearranged letters
curious means odd or strange, so the letters are put in an odd order

parts.note: he is a man in pronoun form

explanation.surface: A peculiar sort of regard, where a fellow comes to feel revulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curious' gives TCREEPS and 'in which' slots the man in after its first letter; 'gets' is only a link. 'Curious' reads as an adjective on respect, hiding its job.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the creeps is an idiom for feeling uneasy disgust or revulsion.

clue.text: European lake giving one 17

parts.note: Lake Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A lake in Europe that sends shivers down your spine.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 across is THE CREEPS, so the definition means spooky.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spooky or uncanny makes your flesh crawl with unease.

clue.text: Section of treaty requiring clergy group to attend party

indicators.note: the clergy group comes along to the party, sitting beside it after it

parts.note: a social is a party or gathering
a chapter is the body of canons of a cathedral

explanation.surface: Part of an international agreement obliges a cathedral's clergy to show up at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The Social Chapter was the part of the EU's Maastricht Treaty covering employment rights.
explanation.definitionFit: The Social Chapter was the employment-rights protocol in the 1992 Maastricht Treaty.

clue.text: Conspicuous net deployed around hole in ground

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around the second piece
deployed means spread out or arranged, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a mine is a hole dug in the ground

explanation.surface: A highly visible net is spread around a pit in the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' gives ENT, and 'around' wraps those letters about the hole so it sits between the E and the NT; 'Conspicuous' is a fair stretch for prominent.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent means standing out or prominent, which is a near synonym for conspicuous.

clue.text: Level a baby clings to?

parts.note: a nursing infant holds on to its mother's breast

explanation.surface: A flat surface for an infant to hang on to?
explanation.definitionFit: To be abreast is to be side by side, level with someone.

clue.text: Judge wise men, honest sounding

indicators.note: the pieces are said aloud and give a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the Magi were the wise men of the Nativity; straight means honest

explanation.surface: Assessing the Magi, who seem to be truthful.
explanation.definitionFit: A magistrate is a judicial officer who judges minor cases in a lower court.

clue.text: Small child a danger for driver

parts.note: a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A little youngster is a hazard to someone at the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A skid is a loss of grip on the road, a real hazard for motorists.

clue.text: My go-cart test is abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means wild or unrestrained, so the letters run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's kart trial has been called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' rearranges GOCARTTEST. 'My' is an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dated exclamations of astonishment, like gosh or goodness me.

clue.text: Revered figure's heavenly food taken round party

definitions.note: read as Revered figure is, the 's standing for is

indicators.note: the food wraps round the party, enclosing it

parts.note: manna was the food sent from heaven to the Israelites
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A saint's divine bread is passed around at a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: The Madonna is the Virgin Mary, venerated in Christian worship.

clue.text: Elephant is not one to bother about new tusk being incomplete

indicators.note: the synonym goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to care is to bother about something

indicators.note: the synonym is missing its last letter

parts.note: ivory is the material of a tusk, and the tusk itself

explanation.surface: The elephant is no meat-eater, so why fret over a fresh tusk being partial?
explanation.walkthrough: 'being incomplete' gives IVOR and 'about' wraps the worry round N plus that. The definition is a whole phrase: elephants eat plants, so they are not meat-eaters.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephants are herbivores, so they are not meat-eaters.

clue.text: African capital almost cold: put this on?

indicators.note: almost the whole word, losing its final letter

parts.note: Tunis is the capital of Tunisia
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: In a chilly North African capital, should you wear this?
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts TUNIS to TUNI. The definition hints at a garment someone would put on.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunic is a loose garment, something worn and so put on.

clue.text: Train preacher to dance for queen

indicators.note: dancing makes the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Coaching a clergyman to dance for a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine Parr was the sixth and last wife of Henry VIII, hence a queen of England.

clue.text: Chirpy type finds painful spasm alien

parts.note: a crick is a painful stiffness of the neck or back
ET is the extraterrestrial of the film

explanation.surface: A cheerful person discovers a sharp twinge is from outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket is an insect that chirps, so a chirping creature.

clue.text: Expected to entertain king or other royal

indicators.note: a host entertains guests, holding the piece inside

parts.note: due means expected
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Due to host the king or some other nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal duke is a duke of the royal family, a member of royalty.

clue.text: Put an end to scams in 1 ac

parts.note: to squash something is to put a stop to it
rackets are fraudulent schemes

explanation.surface: Stop the frauds in a sporting contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 ac is 1 across, GAME: the answer is a racket sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Squash rackets is the full name of squash, a sport and therefore a game.

clue.text: No longer to be used religiously when criminal leaves, having done this?

indicators.note: the criminal departs, so those letters are taken out of the longer word

parts.words: No longer to be used religiously
parts.note: a deconsecrated church is no longer in religious use
a con is a convict, a criminal

explanation.surface: A church taken out of religious use, after a crook departs having violated it?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points back to the criminal: having profaned the place.
explanation.definitionFit: To desecrate is to violate something sacred, which a criminal might have done.

clue.text: Wild survival technique requires two conveyances, including horse

indicators.note: the two vehicles include the extra letter between them

parts.note: a bus is a road conveyance
a craft is a vessel, a conveyance on water or in the air
H is slang for heroin, horse

explanation.surface: A survival skill in the wilds calls for two vehicles and a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: H for horse comes from drug slang: both mean heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushcraft is the skill of living and surviving in the wild outdoors.

clue.text: The distance to the sun getting less — about time

indicators.note: the synonym goes about the extra letter, enclosing it

parts.note: easing means lessening

explanation.surface: How far it is to the sun is shrinking, approximately in time.
explanation.walkthrough: The sun rises in the east, so the definition is a playful take on eastward distance.
explanation.definitionFit: An easting is a distance measured eastward on a map, towards where the sun rises.

clue.text: Press without restraint at head of person held in torture instrument

indicators.note: the pieces are held inside the instrument

parts.note: the rack was a device for stretching victims
taken as written

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Unrestrained journalists turn up, with someone's head stuck in a torture device.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat pack is a pushy group of journalists or photographers hounding celebrities.

clue.text: Daisy, unmarried teacher

indicators.note: M stands for married, so unmarried means losing that letter

parts.note: a master is a schoolteacher

explanation.surface: Daisy is a single schoolteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the standard abbreviation for married.
explanation.definitionFit: Asters are flowers of the daisy family.

clue.text: Join a lot of water marks

parts.note: a sea is a large body of water
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Join a body of water that leaves stains.
explanation.definitionFit: A seam is the line where two pieces are joined together.
